title: Gladia to join OVH Groupe, accelerating Europe's sovereign voice AI ambitions
content:
The transaction would bring Gladia's speech-to-text technology, voice models, and team into OVH Groupe. Gladia will continue to operate as an independent product line under its own brand — with the same API and the same direct relationship with its customers and partners. 
Combined with more than two decades of infrastructure expertise from OVH Groupe — over 500,000 servers across 46 data centers on four continents — the deal gives Gladia's product line a direct path to more compute capacity for lower-latency real-time transcription, greater resilience, and deeper European data residency guarantees, as well as the ability to innovate at a much larger scale. 
"This is the moment we've been building toward since day one," said Jean-Louis Quéguiner, founder and CEO of Gladia. "I spent more than five years at OVHcloud before starting Gladia — it's where my journey in AI began, and where I worked alongside some of the most talented people I've ever met. Coming back this way, with the entire Gladia team, our product, and our independence intact, genuinely feels we’ve come full circle. Together with OVH Groupe, we're going to help shape what European AI will become: sovereign, full-stack, and built to compete with the world's biggest players. None of this would exist without the customers and partners who trusted us from day one, and we intend to keep earning that trust every day."
Building Europe's voice layer, together
The deal follows OVHcloud's acquisition of OVHai LLM (originally founded in 2011 under the name Lingua Custodia, then known as Dragon LLM) earlier this year, which marked the launch of OVHcloud's AI Lab — an initiative dedicated to training and fine-tuning the next generation of sovereign generative, agentic, and multimodal AI. With Gladia, that lab gains its voice layer: a full-stack API to process, understand, and structure audio across more than 100 languages, already embedded in products from companies including HeyGen, Livestorm, Selectra, Circleback, Recall.ai, Noota, and Leexi.
The acquisition also clears a path to native voice AI services distributed through OVHcloud and OVHai to a global customer base of 1.7 million, enabling Gladia to go head-to-head with the largest players in the industry.
What this means for Gladia customers and partners
- No action needed. Your account, integrations, and API remain exactly as they are today.
- Gladia stays Gladia. The product continues to operate as its own independent line, under its own brand, with the same team you know — not folded into or replaced by another platform.
- Same team, same roadmap. The people you work with, the product you rely on, and the pace of development don't change.
- Contracts and pricing are unaffected. Existing agreements and SLAs continue to be honored. Any future changes will be communicated well in advance, never sprung on you.
- More resources to accelerate innovation. Backing from one of Europe's largest cloud infrastructure providers means faster scaling, stronger resilience, and more innovation, with full EU data sovereignty by design.
- More detail to come. Gladia and OVHcloud will share more on joint offerings and deeper integrations in the coming weeks. Questions in the meantime can go to our support team.
About Gladia
Founded in Paris in 2022, Gladia is a French AI company specializing in voice AI, offering speech-to-text transcription and audio intelligence. Through a single API, its platform processes conversations in real time and in batch across more than 100 languages, turning raw audio into structured, actionable data for voice agents, meeting assistants, and contact-center platforms. Gladia is trusted by more than 300,000 developers and 2,000 enterprise customers, including HeyGen, Livestorm, Selectra, Circleback, Recall.ai, Noota, and Leexi.
About OVH Groupe
OVHcloud is a global player and Europe’s leading cloud provider. For more than 25 years, the Group has been putting its technological expertise at the service of businesses, developers and public organizations, developing innovative solutions in cloud, artificial intelligence, quantum and next-generation infrastructure. With 46 data centers around the world, OVHcloud supports 1.7 million customers in more than 140 countries across 4 continents. Its unique integrated model allows it to offer a sovereign, sustainable, high-performance and transparent cloud, designed to address critical challenges of availability, resilience, security, compliance and cost control. In a world where technology increasingly shapes our future, OVHcloud stands by a strong conviction: innovation must remain open, under control and accessible to as many people as possible. By giving organizations the means to retain control of their data and their technology choices, OVHcloud helps them innovate, build and freely deploy the digital world of tomorrow.
Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed. The acquisition remains subject to customary regulatory approvals and closing conditions.

report.summary: OVH Groupe acquires French voice AI startup Gladia, keeping it as an independent brand while adding speech-to-text to Europe's sovereign AI stack.
report.background: Europe has spent years trying to cut its dependence on American hyperscalers for AI models and compute, pushed by GDPR, the EU AI Act, and public-sector procurement rules. Speech is a strategic part of that stack: transcription and voice agents sit at the front door of most enterprise AI workflows, yet the leading APIs largely run on US clouds. Gladia, founded in Paris in 2022, built a multilingual speech-to-text API used by over 300,000 developers. OVHcloud, Europe's largest cloud provider with 46 data centers and 1.7 million customers, launched its AI Lab this year after acquiring OVHai LLM (formerly Lingua Custodia/Dragon LLM). Gladia now supplies the missing voice layer, and its CEO previously spent five years at OVHcloud.
key_points: Gladia stays independent. It will operate as a standalone product line under its own brand, keeping the same API, team, and roadmap. Existing contracts, pricing, and SLAs are unaffected, and customers are told no action is needed. Financial terms were not disclosed, and the deal still requires customary regulatory approvals.

OVHcloud's infrastructure becomes Gladia's engine. Access to more than 500,000 servers across 46 data centers on four continents should cut latency for real-time transcription, improve resilience, and strengthen European data residency guarantees — a meaningful selling point for regulated industries and public-sector buyers.

The move completes a full-stack sovereign AI pitch. After the OVHai LLM acquisition, OVHcloud now owns infrastructure, language models, and voice. Gladia's single API handles more than 100 languages and already powers products from HeyGen, Livestorm, Selectra, Circleback, Recall.ai, Noota, and Leexi.

Distribution is the real prize. OVHcloud's 1.7 million customers across 140 countries give Gladia a direct route into enterprise and government accounts, letting it take on US incumbents such as Deepgram, AssemblyAI, and OpenAI's Whisper-based services on European home turf.

This is a template for European AI consolidation: a well-funded startup with strong developer traction sells to a domestic cloud giant rather than a US hyperscaler, trading some independence for scale, compute, and a built-in distribution channel neither side could easily replicate alone.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this is another signal that sovereign AI is consolidating around regional cloud champions rather than standalone model vendors. OVHcloud can now pitch a complete European alternative — compute, LLMs, and voice — to buyers who cannot or will not send audio to US clouds, pressuring Deepgram, AssemblyAI, and hyperscaler APIs in regulated sectors. For developers, the API surface does not change today, but pricing, roadmap priorities, and deeper OVHcloud integrations are worth watching over the next few quarters. For regular users, the practical effect is likely better real-time transcription, stronger EU privacy guarantees, and more European voice assistants and meeting tools built on infrastructure they may never see.
report.tools: To follow this space, watch Gladia's API and OVHcloud AI Endpoints for sovereign inference; compare with OpenAI Whisper, faster-whisper, and NVIDIA Parakeet/NeMo for self-hosted speech-to-text, and Deepgram or AssemblyAI for managed alternatives. For serving models on your own European infrastructure, look at vLLM, Hugging Face Text Generation Inference, and WhisperX for fast diarized transcription. Recall.ai and Noota are useful references for how voice APIs get embedded into meeting and contact-center products.
